analysis.title: CTA Update
key_insights: CTAs were signaled to move to 'max short' SPX on the prior day's selloff, joining existing 'max short' positions in NDX and RTY. Citi estimates about $15bn unlevered notional of selling over the next 5 sessions.
CTAs could halt SPX selling and move back to moderately short if SPX rallies above 7474 (+0.5% vs 7439 ESZ6). Cover triggers for NDX (28670, +4.6%) and RTY (2856, +4.2%) are much higher.
SX5E is the sole remaining CTA equity long. The flip-short level of 6295 (VGZ6 ref 6302) is within 15bps of the current level, so a small decline would flip CTAs short.
EM and Japan equities are 'max short'. The furthest cover levels globally are MXEF at 1654 (+10.4% vs 1498) and NKY at 62719 (+6.5% vs 58900).
CTAs are back to 'max short' across the US Treasury curve after duration sold off following last week's higher-than-expected CPI report. Cover levels are 102-04 in TU, 106-05 in TY and 107-30 in WN.
In Europe, CTAs are moderately short Bunds and BTPs and 'max short' Gilts and OATs. They add to Bund and BTP shorts below 121.62 (RXZ6 ref 122.06) and 112.39 (IKZ6 ref 112.65).
JGBs are the sole CTA fixed income long. The flip-short level of 126.20 (JBZ6 ref 126.24) is only just below the current level.
Commodity positioning is unchanged, with a moderate long in Oil and 'max short' in Gold and Silver. Oil flips short at 80.95 (-6% vs 86.24 CLZ6) and goes 'max long' at 89.00 (+3.2%).
Gold and Silver need large rallies before CTAs cover, with first buy levels at 4248 in Gold (+9.9% vs 3865) and 60.32 in Silver (+26.8% vs 47.57).

CTAs are 'max long' USD in all six pairs tracked as the DXY extends to YTD highs. The closest USD sell signals are USDJPY at 63.42 (JYZ6 ref 62.92) and GBPUSD at 133.84 (BPZ6 ref 131.90), and EURUSD is much further at 1.1385 (ECZ6 ref 1.0999).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hot CPI print drove a Treasury selloff last week and pushed CTAs back to 'max short' duration.

risk_factors: Many of this week's risk events are still ahead, so a rally could stop CTA SPX selling.
SX5E and JGB flip-short levels are very close to spot, so a small move could trigger CTA selling.
A bounce in Treasuries from current levels would trigger short covering above the stated TU, TY and WN levels.
CTA positioning estimates come from a proprietary model and may not reflect actual CTA positions or returns.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs are 'max short' SPX, NDX and RTY. SX5E is the only equity long and is close to flipping short.
Citi estimates $15bn of unlevered SPX selling over the next 5 sessions to add to shorts.
SPX CTA selling could pause above 7474, and NDX and RTY cover triggers are 4.6% and 4.2% above spot.
CTAs are 'max short' US Treasuries and 'max long' USD across all six pairs, and 'max short' Gold and Silver.
Citi's model has four regimes: max short, moderately short, moderately long and max long. 'Max' does not mean a historical max.
